mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits (HOUST) signals strong housing market activity that precedes corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: HOUST shows three consecutive monthly increases but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals tightening monetary policy that compresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains above 4.0% for two months but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in over 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increases in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signal a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises concurrently but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial production slowdowns (INDPRO < 110), manufacturing weakness signals reduced corporate output and earnings pressure, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains below 110 for three months but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in over 50% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates persistent price pressures that prompt monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL increases for three months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When residential investment (RSAFS) exceeds $380 billion, it signals robust housing activity that supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS exceeds $380 billion but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in over 60% of months.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent rises in residential construction (HOUST) and declines in industrial output (INDPRO) signal a housing-led economic shift that boosts consumer spending and equity returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: HOUST rises and INDPRO falls simultaneously but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In tight labor markets (UNRATE < 4.5%), wage pressures from low unemployment boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE remains below 4.5% for three months but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in over 50% of periods.
